purpose: Phase 4 configuration federation, Phase 5 safety controls, Phase 5F Feishu migration, Phase 7.1 Codex-native permission authority, Phase 7.2 project/chat control, and Phase 7.3A project-shared context bootstrap inventory.

groups.notes: Ask/auto/full are conversation-scoped Codex-native execution modes. Full additionally requires the paired owner and the Mac-local FLORAL_REMOTE_MODE_CEILING=full startup ceiling. The ceiling is not a model-owned permission surface and is stripped from the Codex child environment. MCP authorization and artifact DLP remain independent.

groups.notes: Rolling request/token/cost budgets are enforced before DeepSeek provider attempts. Cost estimates use provider-returned cache hit/miss/output usage and operator-reviewed price coefficients.

FLORAL_WORKSPACE_ROOT is a Mac-local trust boundary and is not projected into config/floral.toml. Projects are real direct-child directories. Project creation bootstraps Codex-native AGENTS guidance plus read-mostly .floral shared context. Chat history remains Codex-owned; FLORAL stores only selected project and per-project active thread IDs.

groups.notes: The native/default Codex fail-safe remains read-only/never while FLORAL starts controlled turns with workspaceWrite + untrusted. Phase 7.1A supports reviewer=user (ask) and reviewer=auto_review (auto) without widening the workspaceWrite sandbox. Native command/file approvals and item/permissions/requestApproval remain Codex protocol decisions; FLORAL authenticates the remote owner and forwards approved turn/session scope without inventing a second permission profile format.
No passthrough is enabled in Phase 4.0A. Each key requires installed-version schema validation and locked-key filtering.

hardcodedDecisions.needle: Planned MCP server cannot be enabled before an active adapter exists
hardcodedDecisions.risk: Vision and macOS MCP transports remain disabled until their adapters are implemented even though the Phase 5.2 authorization boundary now exists.

hardcodedDecisions.needle: MCP parent environment inheritance is forbidden
hardcodedDecisions.risk: Each MCP child receives only explicitly rendered environment entries and must not inherit unrelated credentials.
QQ runtime options adoption must remain observable and support explicit emergency rollback.
SearXNG unified preparation must keep reviewed-image validation, bounded runtime observation, and explicit legacy recovery.
Remote approval must never be delegated to an operator/viewer by configuration drift.
Codex, not FLORAL, classifies native command escalation. FLORAL must still authenticate role and approval scope before forwarding an owner decision in ask mode.

Structured filesystem/network grants can widen a turn or session. FLORAL may only return the validated permission subset that Codex requested, and only after the owner-scoped ask-mode approval path; absent a handler the request fails closed.

hardcodedDecisions.needle: Active MCP tool has no FLORAL capability mapping
hardcodedDecisions.risk: An enabled MCP tool must not bypass role and approval policy merely because it appears in the upstream allowlist.

Native Codex config remains never/read-only; FLORAL sends pinned Codex app-server 0.146.1 approvalPolicy=untrusted with the valid app-server v2 workspaceWrite sandbox encoding, cwd-only/network-disabled and reviewer=user; the stale README approval value unlessTrusted is not used as the wire contract.
Remote write approval is allowed only for a concrete Codex file-change request and must not widen the base read-only sandbox for other capabilities.
Mac-local decisions must remain private, process-session bound, expiring, and one-shot; stale decision files must not survive service restart.
Unknown custom model slugs fall back to Codex metadata without apply_patch; FLORAL must pin a private startup model catalog so concrete file changes can reach the approval broker.
The production transport depends on the SDK behavior proven by the Phase 5F.1 real long-connection probe; version drift must be explicit.
The pinned SDK long-connection lifecycle is isolated so service shutdown remains deterministic even when the SDK connection loop does not expose a reliable close contract.
Remote full access must require an explicit Mac-local startup ceiling in addition to the authenticated owner role.

hardcodedDecisions.needle: Project must be a direct child of the workspace root
hardcodedDecisions.risk: Remote project selection must not turn a project name into arbitrary filesystem path access or follow a symlink outside the Mac-local workspace root.
Project context bootstrap must preserve existing Codex instruction files, avoid symlink/hardlink writes, and remain bounded instead of becoming an unbounded hidden memory prompt.
Initializing shared project context mutates project files and therefore remains owner-only and unavailable while an agent run is active.
